the effect of prior formal and informal education on the academic performance of students enrolled in undergraduate ODL programs in the University of Lagos, Nigeria.

the effect of prior educational background on students’ academic performance in Open and Distance Learning.

students with high level of entry qualifications perform better than those who have lower level of qualifications in both Accounting and Business Administration undergraduate ODL programs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the study revealed that there were significant differences between the performances in the ODL programs of students who were admitted on the basis of their different prior academic backgrounds.
there are significant differences in performance between the students admitted at various levels.

there is no significant difference in the performance of students in the ODL programs at the University of  Lagos, between the various levels of entry qualifications, except for those students admitted on the basis of high performance at relevant higher diplomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of students in the first year of undergraduate ODL programs at the University of Nigeria is significantly affected by their entry qualifications and academic background.
students with higher qualifications and better academic performances in their previous programs are likely to perform better in ODL programs.

the students who entered into the undergraduate ODL programs with prior professional qualifications and high level performance at higher diploma programs performed better than those with lower level qualifications and performance at the first level of the undergraduate ODL program.
